title: It fails before any network activity — that rules out the server
explanation: `ssh apphost 'echo hi'` failing instantly, with no connection delay and no host-key prompt, means sshd on the other end never even saw a TCP packet. Every other directive that could reject a login (AllowUsers, StrictModes on the server's authorized_keys, PubkeyAuthentication) only matters once a connection is actually attempted — so the fault has to be local, on the machine you're sitting on.

title: Read the actual error instead of assuming it's the alias
explanation: Running without swallowing stderr shows `Bad owner or permissions for /home/trainee/.ssh/config`. That's specific: the `ssh` client is refusing to even parse the config file that defines the `apphost` alias, which is why the alias never resolves to anything.

title: The ssh client enforces StrictModes-style paranoia on its own config
explanation: sshd refuses an `authorized_keys` file writable by group/other because anyone with write access could plant a key; the `ssh(1)` client applies the identical logic to your own `~/.ssh/config`, since a writable config could let another local user redirect your connections or inject a `ProxyCommand`. This check runs as your own unprivileged UID — it has nothing to do with root, sshd, or the target host, which is why it's consistent no matter what's on the other end.

title: Confirm the exact permission gap before fixing it
explanation: `ls -l ~/.ssh/config` shows it world-writable (`-rw-rw-rw-`) rather than owner-only — the mode ssh's own check is objecting to, likely left behind by someone loosening permissions the blunt way while chasing an unrelated 'permission denied'.

title: Tighten it and verify with the original failing command
explanation: `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config` restores owner-only access, and `ssh apphost 'echo SSH_OK'` now succeeds — the `apphost` alias resolves and pulls in its `HostName`, `User`, and `IdentityFile` exactly as configured, confirming the client was willing to read the file again.
